summary.intent: Finish the remaining Wave 1 work for the callisto release tooling, then launch a second parallel workflow (Wave 2) covering the status resolver fix, the Python per-declaration locator, false-absent provider reads, and a docs prune, all of which need no decision from the user.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 PRs #222 and #224 merged and #223 is open. The Wave 2 workflow with three implementation lanes and independent reviews was launched on a base of main plus #223. The docs prune (dropping shipped T08-RETRY and T10, rewriting T08) was done in its own worktree and passed `just ci`, but it is not yet committed or opened as a PR.

repo: Wave 1 PRs (#222 E305 pre-baseline conflict, #223 per-declaration Cargo edges as a breaking `minor`, #224 status/version resolver divergence tests) are independent on main and each passes `just ci` alone.

The workspace spec says a non-primary manifest's own name must resolve and a qualified name with no such manifest must fail. `status` violates this and `version` is correct, so aligning `status` is a spec-backed bug fix rather than a D01 policy choice.
`PackageId::resolve_unique` is public API in a published crate, so it should be deprecated rather than removed.
The Python dependency handling follows only the first declaration of a requirement declared twice (extras or markers). It needs the same per-declaration `DepLocator` design as Cargo (#223).

False 'remote absent' reads: a local tag lookup treats any non-zero exit (such as 128) as Absent, and the npm provider matches the substring `e404` in free text. A lookup failure must never mint an absent proof, since that triggers an effect attempt.
W4 follow-ups: the `Timeout` cause is never produced in production, and `Unauthorized`, `RateLimited` and `Unreachable` causes are missing.

Planning docs (ROAD-TO-V1.md, V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json, V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md) still listed shipped SYS-RETRY/SYS-BARRIER/SYS-NAPI work (T08-RETRY, T10). T08 stays because its single-owner effect dedupe is not done.
workflow: Stack lanes that depend on unmerged PRs by building the shared base tree as main plus the open PR branch (here #223 for the Python lane).
Keep the base tree untouched while reviewers diff against it, and do side work such as the docs prune in a separate worktree.

Agents in workflows can't commit and have had connection drops, so they leave work uncommitted, are told to stay in scope and stop around 35 minutes with a report, and the user finishes and verifies commits, changesets, gates and PRs.
Check a gate's own exit line (`exit=0`) rather than inferring success from the notification.
Edit markdown directly and use small scripts for structured JSON edits such as the plan file.

friction: Earlier workflow failures and connection drops forced a conservative approach: agents can't commit and must be time-boxed.
The agent first wrongly held the status resolver fix for D01 and corrected itself later.
About ten stale agent and session worktrees (`wf_*`, `r1-walk-build`, `wave1-stack`) sit under `.claude/worktrees`. They can't be removed yet because some hold the only copy of finished work.
Several runs of PR-state checks were needed to establish which Wave 1 PRs had merged.
open_items: Wave 2 lane results (status resolver, Python locator, false-absent reads) are awaiting implementation and review checks before anything is committed.
Commit and open a PR for the docs prune, which passed `just ci` in the docs-prune-2 worktree.
Merge #223 and the release PR #221, which will pick up #222 and #223 (#223 is a breaking `minor`).
Clean up stale worktrees and merged local branches after the PRs land.

Blocked on the user: D01 (historical owner join and per-document wire policy, then W8 SYS-MATURIN and the rest of W9), the W3 hash-absence and retained-bytes design (then W4 closed types), the Python dev groups policy, and per-branch deletion confirmation including the W0 branch and six unclear ones.
W11 hosted verification needs credentials and an approved run.
The W4 follow-ups (wire the `Timeout` cause, add `Unauthorized`/`RateLimited`/`Unreachable`) are not yet started.
